solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Revealing regrettable act in two different records

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the regrettable act goes inside the second record

parts.note: a written record is a log
a sin is a regrettable act

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a bad deed caught on two separate recordings.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, records, has to be read twice in two different senses: the kind you play and the kind a ship's captain keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making a secret known is revealing it.

clue.text: Home evidently not cleaned without right diligence

indicators.note: an old sense of without is outside, as in 'there is a green hill far away, without a city wall'

parts.note: dust is the evidence nobody has cleaned

explanation.surface: A grubby house suggests the occupant has no diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: "Without" reads as lacking, but here it means outside: the right goes in the middle of the dusty word, not away.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: steady hard work and application, as in 'praised for her industry'.

clue.text: Man successful when racing green cycles around

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round in a loop, so the front letter travels round to the back

explanation.surface: An eco-minded cyclist does well in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is the British runner who won Olympic 1500m gold twice. Cycles belongs to the racing picture but is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the double Olympic champion was indeed a man who succeeded at racing.

clue.text: Daisy Duck getting cross, I heard

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, O
a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: what is heard is only a sound, so I stands for a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the organ of sight, said the same as I

explanation.surface: Daisy Duck, Donald's girlfriend, loses her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Duck reads as one cartoon name, but Daisy alone is the definition and Duck gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tall white-petalled meadow flower is one kind of daisy.

clue.text: Lacking time, change tiny bit of cash at first in town

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of in

parts.note: P, a penny, is a tiny amount of cash

indicators.note: Lacking says the word for change is missing the letter for time

explanation.surface: Someone short of time changes a tiny coin first thing in town.
explanation.walkthrough: SWITCH without T gives SWICH, behind I and P. Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich is a large town in Suffolk, in eastern England.

clue.text: Our distant relatives consume fruit drinks

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside itself, so the fruit takes in the word for consume

explanation.surface: Our relatives at a party get through the fruit punch.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fruit drinks" looks like a noun phrase, juices; drinks is really the verb, and fruit its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans share a common ancestor with chimpanzees and gorillas, making them relatives at some evolutionary distance.

clue.text: Piano note organ put out daily

parts.note: the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a newspaper is an organ; the Financial Times comes out daily

explanation.surface: A piano note and an organ are heard every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ belongs to the keyboard picture; in crosswords it often means a newspaper, as a mouthpiece for views.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction: piano on a score tells the player to play quietly.

clue.text: Losing face, Holst struggles with Mars? Yes, in arrangement of The Planets

indicators.note: struggles means wrestles about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
losing face means losing the front, so the first letter of Holst goes

explanation.surface: A composer, humiliated, wrestles with one movement of his orchestral suite The Planets.
explanation.walkthrough: Holst wrote The Planets, whose first movement is Mars; but the definition is the real planets' arrangement. OLST, MARS and YES are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: The solar system is the sun and the planets in their orbits, the cosmic arrangement of planets.

clue.text: Polish maybe experiencing popularity, adopted by school

indicators.note: an adopted child is taken into a family

parts.note: a school is a group of fish

explanation.surface: A Pole is welcomed by a school now that they are popular.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality; lower-case it is a glossy coating on furniture or nails.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by maybe: a polish is one kind of surface coating.

clue.text: Current and potentially endless obstacle to Labour

indicators.note: something potential could become something else, so ENDLESS may turn into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A commentator names the Labour Party's present, never-ending obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with its capital suggests the British party; it only means work, the capital being the first word of the definition's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness gets in the way of work: nobody labours while loafing.

clue.text: Cockney recovering part of capital

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the h sound at the start of words

explanation.surface: A Londoner is getting better after an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are Londoners whose accent drops initial H, so 'healing' becomes 'ealing'. Ealing is a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a borough in west London, so it is one district of the British capital.

clue.text: Cub shedding coat with fur fit for purpose

indicators.note: an animal shedding its coat loses its outer layer, so the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A young animal moulting its fur is ready for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Shedding a coat fits a furry cub so well that it is easy to miss that the word itself is being stripped.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything serviceable enough to be put to work is fit for purpose.

clue.text: Area of commerce functions aboard double-decker?

definitions.meaning: the affairs conducted on a large bus

explanation.surface: A trade sector asks what goes on aboard a double-decker bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second half: a double-decker is a big bus, and what happens on it is its business.
explanation.definitionFit: Large corporations collectively form a sector of commerce; the second sense is a playful literal reading.

clue.text: Grab break after unlimited cold period

indicators.note: after means the break comes after the other piece
unlimited means without its limits, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: Snatch a breather once the endless winter is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone is to catch their attention, as to grab them is in informal use.

clue.text: Violent resistance suppressed by Winnie the Pooh and Snow White characters

parts.note: the bouncing tiger in Winnie the Pooh

explanation.surface: Cartoon favourites put down a violent uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters is plural because it covers both Tigger and the dwarf. Violent resistance looks like one phrase but the definition stops after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose but fair: someone too quick to open fire is inclined to violence.

clue.text: Protecting millions in online financial sector

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Online banks safeguard vast sums.
explanation.walkthrough: Protecting fits the surface's talk of keeping money safe; the answer protects land by building banks along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: raising a bank of earth shields land from flooding.

clue.text: Barkeeper is attractive character in melodramatic series?

parts.note: a dish is a good-looking person

explanation.surface: The pub landlord is the heartthrob of a TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Barkeeper suggests a publican; the question mark allows it to mean something that keeps a bar, of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: the bathroom tray keeps a bar of soap.

clue.text: Embargo is stopping United helping City fans' dream

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the embargo and is plug the helping

explanation.surface: A transfer embargo keeps Manchester United from helping Manchester City supporters get what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: City fans suggests football supporters; here they are simply people who love cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading: someone who loves cities would dream of towns spreading everywhere.

clue.text: Far from cool, short anorak seen on you abroad

indicators.note: seen on means placed above in a down clue, so the first piece sits on top
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, a nerd

explanation.surface: Someone shivering in a short coat that is worn by you overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anorak' looks like the coat; in Britain it is also slang for an obsessive enthusiast. In a down clue 'seen on' puts the first piece on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means anxious and tense, the opposite of being cool and calm.

clue.text: Undemanding job's axed in firm

indicators.note: whatever is axed is chopped out, here the letters IN

parts.note: a paid post needing little work

explanation.surface: An easy post has been cut at a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company; it is the adjective. The 's is short for is: the easy job has IN axed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something fixed fast and stable is firm.

clue.text: Implore daughter leaving meal's starter

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for daughter goes away from the word for meal

explanation.surface: Someone pleads as their daughter leaves the table before the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like the first course of the meal, but here it means a novice. BEG plus INNER, DINNER without D.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is someone just starting out, a novice.

clue.text: Is a hip-hopper keeping cover of Eminem in charts again?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the rapping word holds the Eminem letters inside
a cover wraps the outside, so the outer letters of Eminem are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of EMINEM

explanation.surface: A question about a rapper covering an Eminem song that re-enters the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover and charts both belong to the pop picture: a cover version, the hit parade. Here charts is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts as a verb means maps; doing it again is the re- prefix.

clue.text: Gold going up and down dresses heading for Tina Turner

indicators.note: dresses means clothes, so the gold letters wrap round the letter

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry; written going up it reads RO, then going down it reads OR

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of Tina

explanation.surface: Gold lamé going up and down dresses the singer Tina Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the surname; it is the definition, something that turns. Gold is OR in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, so literally a thing that turns.

clue.text: Murmur Tudor ruler gets components for arms

parts.note: Elizabeth I: ER (Elizabeth Regina) plus I

explanation.surface: A Tudor monarch quietly acquires weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Arms suggests weapons, which suits a monarch; here they are limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper-arm bones, one in each arm, are components of the limbs.

clue.text: Another broadcast occupied by one broadcasting

indicators.note: occupied by means having something inside, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A second programme goes out, with one person presenting it.
explanation.walkthrough: ANOTHER rearranged gives ONTHEAR, and I goes in between A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: On the air is the idiom for being transmitted on radio or television at the moment.

clue.text: Every second of service pleases pious priest

indicators.note: the second letter of every following word is taken

explanation.surface: Each moment of a church service delights a devout clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second reads as each moment in time; it means the second letter of each following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical figure: the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel.

clue.text: It could give you a better view of French city

definitions.text: It could give you a better view
definitions.meaning: a curved glass that magnifies or focuses

explanation.surface: Something that offers a fine outlook over a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Of looks like part of 'view of French city'; it only joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses and cameras sharpen what you see; the French town is in the Pas-de-Calais.

clue.text: Try extremely short article penned by conservative in Reform

parts.note: to have a go is to try

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only the outer letters of short
something penned is shut in a pen, so A is enclosed by the conservative word

explanation.surface: A brief piece by a Conservative writer about the Reform party.
explanation.walkthrough: Reform with its capital suggests the political party; it is the verb, as an offender might reform.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a criminal who gives up crime and lives honestly has reformed.
